A safety and compliance tracker keeps inspections, incident reports and certificates in one place, and it warns you before anything expires. This guide shows how to build one without code in[Taskade Genesis](https://www.taskade.com/ai/apps) , four other ways to do it, and when each one is the better fit. For the renewal side of the same job, read[how to automate license renewals](https://www.taskade.com/blog/automate-license-renewals) .


## Quick answer


To build a safety compliance tracker without code, list every certificate, license and inspection with an owner and an expiry date. Add a checklist for inspections and a form for incidents, and set alerts at 90 and 30 days. SafetyCulture's free plan covers up to 10 seats and 5 inspection templates. Taskade Genesis puts the register, the checklists, the incident form and an assistant that answers from your manual in one app.


The rest of this page covers what each part does, the three steps to build it, what to track, who sees what, a worked example, what it costs, four other ways to do it, and the limits to know before an audit.


## What a compliance tracker needs


A compliance tracker needs five parts, and together they keep an audit calm. A register gives every certificate an owner and an expiry date. Inspection checklists hold the evidence. An incident form catches problems the day they happen. Alerts arrive before each deadline, and quick answers come from your own procedures.


Part What it looks like How Taskade does it


Register "Fire extinguisher service, owner: site lead, expires 14 Mar" A Certificates project with owner, issue date, expiry date and status


Inspection checklist Monthly vehicle check, 12 items, photo of the tyres A checklist project per inspection, with an upload field for photos


Incident form "Slip in the loading bay, 09:40, no injury" A published form that adds a row to the Incident log


Expiry alerts 90 days and 30 days before the date A daily Schedule trigger, Find Task(s), Assign Task and an email


Answers from the manual "What do we do after a chemical spill?" An AI agent with the manual in its knowledge


The diagram shows how the three inputs meet in one app and what goes out each morning.


### The expiry board in three bands


The expiry board is the screen the team opens every morning. It sorts every item into a band, so nobody reads dates one by one.


```text
+----------------------+----------------------+----------------------+
|  EXPIRED          2  |  WITHIN 30 DAYS   3  |  WITHIN 90 DAYS   5  |
+----------------------+----------------------+----------------------+
| First-aid kit refill | Forklift license     | Gas safety cert      |
|   owner: site lead   |   owner: ops lead    |   owner: facilities  |
|   expired 3 days ago |   due in 12 days     |   due in 61 days     |
| Ladder inspection    | Hull survey          | Insurance renewal    |
|   owner: crew chief  |   owner: captain     |   owner: finance     |
|   expired 1 day ago  |   due in 27 days     |   due in 88 days     |
|                      | Food hygiene cert    | ...                  |
+----------------------+----------------------+----------------------+
Action today         Book the renewal       Plan and budget


```


### What goes in the register


The register is one project with one row per certificate, license or inspection. Ten fields cover most small teams.


Field Example Why it matters


Item Fire extinguisher service What the auditor asks for


Type Certificate, license, inspection, training Lets you filter the board


Site or asset Warehouse 2, Vessel 1, Van 4 Answers "is this site covered?"


Owner The person's email The alert goes to this person


Issued 2025-03-14


Proof of the last renewal


Expires 2026-03-14


The daily check reads this date


Renews every 12 months Sets the next expiry when you upload the new certificate


Keep record until 5 years after the year it covers Tells you when an old record can leave the register


Evidence The PDF or a photo The auditor wants the document


Status Active, Expiring Soon, Expired Sets the band on the board


The free[risk register template](https://www.taskade.com/templates/risk-register) covers the risk side of the same job, and the[maintenance templates](https://www.taskade.com/templates/maintenance) cover planned checks on equipment.


### Real compliance apps that customers run


Two anonymised patterns from teams that run safety work on Taskade Genesis show how different the same job looks:


- A US tour-boat operator gives crews one Taskade Genesis safety portal for 3 inspected vessels. An assistant answers from the captain's manual, and each certificate turns red 30 days before it expires.
- A UK travel-safety service gives travelers a Taskade Genesis app behind access codes, with threat-response steps, local safety advice and post-incident reports. It runs about 40 automations a month.


The first is a register with an assistant. The second is an incident and response app for people in the field. The build below starts with the register and adds the incident form, so it supports both.


## Before you build: list what you must track


Write the obligation list before you build the register, because a tracker only warns about items it holds. Walk each site and each role, and list every certificate, license, inspection and training record with its owner and its renewal interval. The table below shows the areas most small businesses start with.


Area Typical items How often (check your local rule) Usual owner


Fire safety Extinguisher service, alarm test, fire exit walk Monthly walk, yearly service Site lead


First aid Kit contents, first-aider certificates Monthly kit check, certificate by its date Named first-aider


Equipment and vehicles Forklift, ladders, vans, lifting gear Before use, monthly or by hours Ops lead


Licenses and permits Trading, food hygiene, waste carrier, vessel By the date on the license Owner or manager


Insurance Liability, vehicle, property Yearly Finance


Training Induction, manual handling, refreshers At start, then by the course date HR or manager


Incident records Injury and near-miss reports The day it happens Safety lead


Some records also carry a legal retention period. In the US, many employers with more than 10 employees must record work-related injuries and illnesses on OSHA Forms 300, 300A and 301, and keep them for five years after the end of the year they cover ([OSHA recordkeeping](https://www.osha.gov/recordkeeping) , checked 2026-10-19). Other countries set their own rules, so check with your regulator and put the period in the "Keep record until" field.


Rank the list by risk before you load it. Put items that stop work when they lapse (a vehicle inspection, a food hygiene certificate, liability insurance) at the top, and give each one a backup owner.


## Build it in Taskade in 3 steps


You build the compliance tracker in three steps: clone a working register app, load your items and your manual, then switch on the alerts and incident routing. The register is the part that takes time, because you collect dates from many places. The automations take minutes.


For the click-by-click version, follow the[compliance tracker tutorial](https://www.taskade.com/learn/genesis/compliance-tracker) in Learn Taskade.


### Step 1: Clone the license and certificate tracker


[Clone the License Manager app](https://www.taskade.com/app/license-manager-dashboard-rlfk7lsd3kxtla1z?action=clone&utm_source=landing_blog&utm_medium=howto&utm_campaign=build-compliance-tracker) and pick a workspace. Taskade copies the app and its projects into that workspace. The License Manager already sorts every item into Expired, Expiring Soon and Active bands, with filters and a history tab. It ships with software licenses as sample data, so you rename the entries to your certificates and inspections. The copy counts as one Taskade Genesis app on your plan.


Try the live app below before you clone it:


Next, add the inspection and incident parts. You can add projects and a form by hand, or describe them to Taskade EVE in the prompt box. For example:


> Turn this into a safety and compliance tracker. Add a Certificates register with owner, issue date, expiry date and status bands Expired, 30 days and 90 days. Add an Inspections checklist with photo evidence and an Incident report form that assigns the safety lead. Add an assistant that answers from our safety manual.


A prompt that changes the app uses[AI credits](https://www.taskade.com/learn/genesis/model-credits) . On Free, you earn free AI credits with referrals and invites, and you can upgrade any time. Pro includes 50,000 AI credits a month. Edits by hand use no credits. The[first app guide](https://www.taskade.com/learn/genesis/first-app) walks through the editor.


### Step 2: Load your register and your manual


Collect your certificates in a spreadsheet first, one row per item, with the ten fields from the table above. Then[import the CSV](https://www.taskade.com/learn/import/csv-import) into the Certificates project. Most teams find dates in three places: the folder of PDFs, the supplier emails, and the walls of the site.


Upload your safety manual and your procedures to the agent's[knowledge](https://www.taskade.com/learn/agents/knowledge) . The agent then answers from your own files: what to do after a fall, who signs off a hot-work permit, or which form a driver fills after a near miss. Keep the manual as the source of truth, and update the file when the procedure changes. PDF uploads need a paid plan, and a Free agent takes one knowledge source. On Free, paste the procedures into one project and add that project instead.


For inspections, add one checklist project per inspection type, for example a monthly vehicle check or a weekly fire exit walk. Add an upload field so inspectors attach a photo to each item.[Let people send files to your app](https://www.taskade.com/learn/genesis/app-uploads) shows where each photo lands. A sample checklist:


Item Pass / fail Evidence


Fire exits clear and signed Pass Photo of each exit


Extinguishers in date and in place Pass Photo of the tag


First-aid kit stocked Fail: refill gloves Photo, then a task to the site lead


Spill kit sealed Pass Photo


### Step 3: Turn on expiry alerts and incident routing


Open **Automations** and switch on two automations. The first watches dates. The second routes incidents.


Automation Starts when What it does


1. Expiry check Every day at 07:00 Find Task(s) lists items that expire within 90 and within 30 days, assigns each owner, emails them, and sets the band


2. Incident routing Someone submits the incident form Adds a row to the Incident log, assigns the safety lead, emails them


The expiry check uses the[Schedule](https://www.taskade.com/learn/automation/schedule) trigger with your time zone, and[Find Task(s)](https://www.taskade.com/learn/automation/find-tasks) to list the items. To act on the exact day an item expires, add the[Task Due](https://www.taskade.com/learn/automation/task-due) trigger.[New Due Date](https://www.taskade.com/learn/automation/due-date) reacts when someone sets a new expiry after a renewal. The incident form uses the[AI Forms](https://www.taskade.com/learn/automation/forms-trigger) trigger, and[Assign Task](https://www.taskade.com/learn/automation/assign-task) hands the report to the safety lead.


The sequence below shows one certificate on its way to renewal.


An incident follows its own forward path. Each status change is a field update, so you can add a Logger automation that writes the change to a history project, as in[how to build an approval workflow](https://www.taskade.com/blog/build-approval-workflow) .


Test the tracker with two items before your team uses it:


1. Add a test certificate that expires in 20 days. On the next morning, check that the owner got the email and the item sits in the 30-day band.
2. Submit a test incident from a phone. Check that the safety lead got the email and the Incident log has the row.

## Who sees what


A compliance tracker has four kinds of users, and each one needs a different screen. The safety lead sees everything. A site lead sees the items for one site. Staff see the incident form and the assistant. An auditor reads the register and the evidence without changing them.


Person Sees Can do


Safety lead Every item, every incident, the weekly summary Edit the register, close incidents


Site lead The items and incidents for their site Upload evidence, mark checks done


Staff The incident form and the assistant Report an incident, ask a question


Auditor The register and the evidence Read and export


Inside the workspace, role-based access runs from Owner to Viewer, so the auditor can be a Viewer. In the published app, sign-in confirms who each person is. To show a site lead only one site, match each item to that person's email or site, and test it with a second account.


## Worked example: 3 sites and 64 items


A business with 3 sites, 64 register items and about 5 incidents a month needs about 40 automation runs a month. That is above the 10 runs on Free, and far below the 1,000 runs on Pro. Each automation counts one run from trigger to finish, however many items the daily check finds.


Automation What sets it off Runs a month


Expiry check Once a day 30


Incident routing 5 incident reports 5


Weekly summary Once a week 4


Total 39


Spread across a year, 64 items with yearly renewals give about 5 renewals a month. The 90-day alert gives each owner three months to book each one, so no renewal lands in the last week.


```text
64 items, yearly renewals, 3 sites
Jan  #####   5      Each "#" is one renewal due that month.
Feb  ####    4      The 90-day alert reaches the owner
Mar  ######  6      three months before each bar.
Apr  #####   5
...
Weekly summary: expired 0 | due in 30 days 4 | inspections done 11 of 12


```


The weekly summary carries the three numbers a manager needs: items expired, items due within 30 days, and inspections done against inspections due. If the expired count stays above zero for two weeks, the owner list is the problem, not the dates.

## Limitations: when Taskade is not the right fit


Choose a dedicated safety system (an EHS platform) when a regulator needs official forms, signed sign-offs or offline audits at remote sites. Taskade keeps the register, the alerts and the answers. It does not file reports with a regulator for you.


- **A regulator needs its own report forms.** Taskade has no built-in regulatory report forms. Fill the official form and attach it as evidence.
- **Each sign-off needs a legal e-signature.** Taskade has no DocuSign connector. Approvers confirm in the app.
- **Inspectors work where there is no signal.** Test the checklist on a phone at the site before you depend on it.
- **An auditor must trust a locked record.** A workspace owner can edit any project. Use a system with a locked audit trail.
- **The assistant is not the rule book.** The assistant answers from your documents. Keep the manual as the source of truth and check critical steps against it.


## FAQ


Can I build a compliance tracker without code?


Yes. A compliance tracker needs a register of every certificate, license and inspection with an owner and an expiry date, a checklist for inspections, a form for incidents, and alerts before each deadline. In Taskade Genesis you clone a working register app, rename its entries, and add the inspection and incident parts in plain English.


What should a safety compliance tracker include?


A safety compliance tracker includes a register of every certificate, license, inspection and training record, each with an owner, an expiry date, a renewal interval and the evidence. It also holds inspection checklists with photos, an incident form, and alerts at 90 and 30 days before each date. A weekly summary shows items expired, items due within 30 days, and inspections done against inspections due.


How long should we keep incident records?


It depends on your country and your industry. In the US, many employers with more than 10 employees must keep OSHA Forms 300, 300A and 301 for five years after the end of the year they cover. Put the period in a Keep record until field on each row, and check the rule with your regulator.


How do expiry alerts work?


A scheduled automation runs every morning. It finds every item that expires within 90 days and within 30 days, assigns it to its owner, and emails them. The register shows each item in a band: Expired, Expiring Soon or Active, so the board tells you what needs work today.


Can inspectors fill a checklist on their phone?


Yes. A published Taskade Genesis app opens in a phone browser, and the Taskade mobile apps open the same projects. An upload field on the checklist lets an inspector attach a photo as evidence. Test the full checklist on a phone at the site before you rely on it, in particular where the signal is weak.


Can staff report an incident without a Taskade account?


Yes. Publish the incident form and share its link. Anyone with the link can submit a report, and you can protect the form with a password. Each report adds a row to the Incident log, and an automation assigns it to the safety lead and emails them.


Can the assistant answer from our safety manual?


Yes. Upload the manual and your procedures to the agent's knowledge. The agent answers from those files, for example the steps to follow after a fall or the date a certificate must be renewed. Each answer uses AI credits, PDF uploads need a paid plan, and the manual stays the source of truth.


Who can see incident reports?


You decide. Inside the workspace, role-based access runs from Owner to Viewer. App sign-in works on every plan and confirms who each person is. To show staff only their own reports, match each report to the person's email, and test it with a second account.


How much does a compliance tracker cost in Taskade?


Free has 3 apps, 2 members, 1 agent and 10 automation runs a month, and it starts with no AI credits. A daily expiry check uses a run each day, so a live tracker needs Pro at $10 a month billed annually ($20 monthly), with 1,000 runs, 50,000 AI credits and up to 10 members. Pro also connects up to 10 custom domains, and Business at $25 a month billed annually connects unlimited custom domains.


When is SafetyCulture or Smartsheet the better choice?


SafetyCulture fits teams that run many mobile inspections a day, and its free plan covers up to 10 seats. Smartsheet fits teams that already plan their work in sheets. Pick a dedicated safety system when a regulator needs official forms or signed sign-offs. Pick Taskade Genesis when the register, the alerts and the answers from your manual belong in one app.
